text:
John Carlson spent 1,143 games in Washington, then a 16-game stop in Anaheim, and at 36 he has landed in Tampa Bay looking like a defenseman with plenty left. He has 21 points in 24 games, a pace ahead of last season, and 13 points in his last ten, including a stretch CBS Sports noted of ten points in five games. One of those nights was three assists against the Capitals.

The Lightning are thriving with him out there. At five on five they get about 60% of the expected goals with Carlson on the ice, six points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him 17th of 215 defensemen last season, most of it from even-strength offense.

Some of the scoring is running ahead of itself. He has seven goals on 4.5 expected, shooting 11.9% against a likely range around 8%, so expect fewer pucks to go in. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking also flags the old weak spot: only 31% of his exits keep possession, so the forecheck can still find him. But as a power-play passer and a second-pair driver, this signing looks good so far.
